claims.title: CDN assets are readable in transit over HTTP
claims.description: An on-path attacker between `entity:reader` and `entity:cdn` can intercept `flow:entity:reader>entity:cdn>asset-fetch`, which crosses from the public internet into the CDN zone with `encryption_in_transit` stated absent. The attacker reads images, stylesheets, and downloads served from `store:cdn-bucket`; if downloads contain proprietary or otherwise business-critical content, capture enables offline reuse and reconnaissance without accessing the CDN directly.

severity.justification: Likelihood is high because `flow:entity:reader>entity:cdn>asset-fetch` is a public boundary crossing and HTTP transport protection is stated absent. Impact is medium because the CDN-side assets are tagged `business-critical-data`, though the model does not establish that every asset is sensitive.

mitigations.summary: Serve all CDN assets over HTTPS
mitigations.detail: Require TLS 1.2+ for `flow:entity:reader>entity:cdn>asset-fetch`, redirect HTTP to HTTPS, and prevent plaintext origin or edge delivery.

claims.title: Database maintenance traffic exposes CMS data on the public network
claims.description: An attacker able to observe the public-network path can intercept the direct MySQL session on `flow:entity:admin>store:mysql-database>direct-administration`. This boundary-crossing flow has no TLS and carries pages, accounts, and comments to `store:mysql-database`, including data tagged `pii`. Captured account and content data can be used for targeted attacks against readers and to map the CMS data corpus.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because plaintext observation needs a network-path position, but `flow:entity:admin>store:mysql-database>direct-administration` crosses from `boundary:public-internet` and has stated absent transport encryption. Impact is high because the traffic carries the contents of `store:mysql-database`, which is tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS for MySQL on `flow:entity:admin>store:mysql-database>direct-administration` and validate the database server certificate.
Require administration through a controlled private access path or jump host rather than permitting direct database connections from arbitrary public locations.

claims.title: CMS-to-MySQL traffic may expose account and comment data if transport encryption is absent
claims.description: `flow:process:web-server>store:mysql-database>cms-data` reads and writes pages, accounts, and comments between the internet-facing `process:web-server` and `store:mysql-database`, carrying `pii` and business-critical data. Its `encryption_in_transit` value is unknown. If this internal MySQL connection is not encrypted, an attacker with a foothold on the hosted-network path can intercept the traffic and collect account and content records; those records can then support targeted attacks against site readers. This is conditional on resolving the unknown transport-encryption attribute and does not assert that the connection is plaintext.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:process:web-server>store:mysql-database>cms-data` is unverified and an attacker still needs a hosted-network path position. Impact is high because the flow carries `pii` and reaches `store:mysql-database`, which also holds business-critical CMS data.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce TLS for the CMS database connection
mitigations.detail: Set and verify TLS on `flow:process:web-server>store:mysql-database>cms-data`, including certificate validation, so MySQL payloads are confidential on internal network paths.

claims.title: Asset publication may disclose unpublished CDN content if its transport is unencrypted
claims.description: `process:web-server` publishes newly created assets to `store:cdn-bucket` over `flow:process:web-server>store:cdn-bucket>asset-publish`, a crossing from the hosted network to the CDN zone. The flow's protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the publication channel lacks encryption, an observer on that inter-zone path can intercept assets before or as they are published, potentially obtaining business-critical downloads before intended public release. This is conditional on the unverified protocol and transport protection.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because this is a stated hosted-network-to-CDN boundary crossing but the flow's protocol and transport encryption are unverified. Impact is medium because `store:cdn-bucket` holds business-critical published assets, while the model does not establish that all published assets are confidential.

mitigations.summary: Use an authenticated TLS publication channel
mitigations.detail: Require HTTPS or another mutually authenticated encrypted protocol for `flow:process:web-server>store:cdn-bucket>asset-publish` and verify the CDN endpoint identity.

claims.title: A storage copy could expose CMS accounts if MySQL encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:mysql-database` holds CMS pages, accounts, and comments and is tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, but its `encryption_at_rest` attribute is unknown. If that unknown resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker who obtains a disk, snapshot, backup, or decommissioned storage copy can read the database files without using the CMS or its normal database access path. The copied account and content data enables targeted attacks on readers and disclosure of the site corpus. This is conditional and does not claim that MySQL is presently unencrypted at rest.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:mysql-database` has unverified encryption at rest and the attacker must obtain an operational storage copy. Impact is high because the store is tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, so a raw copy can disclose the database corpus irreversibly.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encryption at rest for MySQL copies
mitigations.detail: Establish the actual `encryption_at_rest` posture of `store:mysql-database`, then require managed-key encryption for database volumes, backups, snapshots, and replicas, with export access restricted.

mitigations.summary: Protect the most sensitive database fields separately
mitigations.detail: Apply field-level encryption or tokenization to account-related PII so a storage-layer copy has less directly readable information.

claims.title: A copied CDN bucket may disclose business-critical assets if it lacks encryption at rest
claims.description: `store:cdn-bucket` holds published images, stylesheets, and downloads tagged `business-critical-data`, while its `encryption_at_rest` attribute is unknown. If encryption at rest is not enabled, anyone obtaining a bucket export, storage backup, or underlying media copy can read the asset collection outside the CDN's serving controls. Such a copy can expose non-public or proprietary downloadable content and support later misuse of the published assets. This draft is conditional on the unresolved at-rest encryption state.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `encryption_at_rest` for `store:cdn-bucket` is unverified and the attacker must obtain a storage copy. Impact is medium because the bucket's assets are tagged `business-critical-data`, but the model does not identify PII, credentials, or other higher-classification content in it.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt CDN bucket contents and operational copies
mitigations.detail: Establish the encryption posture of `store:cdn-bucket`, require managed-key encryption at rest for bucket objects and backups, and restrict export or snapshot permissions.

claims.title: An unauthenticated direct MySQL path could expose the entire CMS database
claims.description: `entity:admin` reaches `store:mysql-database` directly through `flow:entity:admin>store:mysql-database>direct-administration`, but the flow's authentication is unknown. If this externally initiated MySQL path lacks strong authentication or permits overly broad database credentials, an outside attacker can query the same pages, accounts, and comments that the admin maintains and elicit the database corpus. The exposure is especially consequential because the target store is tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`; obtained account data can enable targeting of readers. This is conditional on the unresolved authentication state and does not assert that the database accepts unauthenticated connections.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because authentication on the direct public-origin MySQL flow is unverified, though exploitation requires that the unresolved control be weak or absent. Impact is high because successful queries against `store:mysql-database` disclose data tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data` in bulk.

mitigations.detail: Configure `flow:entity:admin>store:mysql-database>direct-administration` to require strong individual administrator authentication and a least-privilege database role rather than broad shared access.
Restrict MySQL network access to a controlled administration path and log and alert on direct read queries and bulk exports.
